items.body: Cicadas does a beautiful job using an experimental musical lens to help focus our attention on an often overlooked yet fascinating creature who lives in a world completely different from ours, yet that is also exactly the same (a beautiful expression of German phenom​enological biologist Jakob von Uexküll’s concept of the Umwelt or life-world that is specific to the sensory perceptions of each kind of animal). Eerie liquid stringlike sounds lend a darker, horror film soundtrack feel Cicadas: Broods XIX and XIII by Robert Thurman   Groups of cicadas that emerge during the same year in the same North American region on a periodical cycle of 13 or 17 years are known as broods. In 2024 two broods emerged together—the Great Southern Brood known as XIX and the Northern Illinois Brood known as XIII–leading to a massive cicada bloom (or infestation, depending on your point of view) in the areas where the two broods overlapped. As part of his ongoing “Poetic Nature” series of artworks, poems, and musical compositions, Robert R. Thurman crafted Cicadas to memorialize this momentous combined emergence, the first in two centuries. For me Cicadas does a beautiful job using an experimental musical lens to help focus our attention on an often overlooked yet fascinating creature who lives in a world completely different from ours, yet that is also exactly the same (a beautiful expression of German phenom​enological biologist Jakob von Uexküll’s concept of the Umwelt or life-world that is specific to the sensory perceptions of each kind of animal). I love cicadas for their fantastic dinosaur/alien appearance—periodical cicada adults in the genus Magicicada have coal-black bulbous bodies, bright red eyes, orange-veined wings and legs that taper to black at their tips–and for their cascading susurrations of sound that mean summer has truly arrived to North Texas (for photos, recordings, and tons of scientific information you can visit the Periodical Cicada Info Pages. For many of us in the U.S. who grew up listening to annual cicadas (different species than the periodical ones, but similar vibe in sound and appearance) as kids lolling around through long, steamy summer days, their calls bring a certain nostalgia. This nostalgic feeling about summer cicadas is certainly shared by many in Japan judging from how often the calls of cicadas signal poignant moments of transition from youth to adulthood and longing for lost innocence in manga and anime. Thurman’s Cicadas consists of three long tracks, the first two clocking in at about ten minutes each, and the last at fourteen. The album begins with the appropriately named “Emergence.” Brushed, syncopated percussive elements do a great job evoking the unexpected emergence patterns of thousands of individual animals pushing their way to the surface of the soil at slightly different times. Repeated drones that arise later in the track feel a bit like sirens passing on a distant highway, making me think of the bright red eyes of these unnerving-looking creatures. Eerie liquid stringlike sounds lend a darker, horror film soundtrack feel. Periodic flickering and ringing resounds as cicadas buzz past your ears on their inscrutable errands, like busy travelers jostling one another in the airport as they speed their way along. Cicadas buzz past your ears on their inscrutable errands :: On “Aggregations” Thurman leans into the alien invader feel of cicada broods. The sounds here remind me a bit of ELTA Music’s Solar 42 analog drone machine that one of my students used this past semester to evoke a 1950s giant insect film for one of the segments of a cicada-focused soundwalk composition she created. Drones swell and ebb in waves, like male cicadas chorusing to attract females for mating on romantic sunlit treetop branches. Later in the track a phaser-like sound emerges, a laser-focusing beacon sent over the airwaves solely for female cicada listeners. At first the scale feels off-putting: nearly every open surface on each branch and tree-trunk covered with cicadas. But eventually the thick sounds start to feel more familiar and even reassuring, like the summer calls of more well-known annual cicadas. “Chorusing” sounds almost transcendent: a luminous quality resonating as males with their tymbal-scraping calls and females with their wing-flicks respond to each other, duetting in a language of love only their own kind fully understands, yet with an unearthly beauty this track helps all of us appreciate. The listener gets a clear feeling of many insect bodies packed closely together, wings vibrating in choruses of rising tides of excitement followed by calmer periods. By the end the track becomes much quieter as the chorus stills and the massive brood recedes for another 13 or 17 years. Cicadas: Broods XIX and XIII is available on Bandcamp. Cicadas: Broods XIX and XIII by Robert Thurman
items._cn_summary: 这是一张围绕2024年北美双蝉群同时出现这一自然现象创作的实验音乐专辑。 Thurman采用实验音乐与电子声景相结合的手法，用阴郁的弦乐声响与 drones 模拟蝉的生命世界与涌现过程，三首长篇作品分别约10至14分钟，具有当代古典的结构感与概念性。专辑引用了德国生物学家Umwelt理论，探讨不同物种感知世界的差异，同时融入日本动漫中蝉的象征意象，赋予作品跨文化视野。音乐本身以实验性声响设计为核心，捕捉蝉鸣与自然的微妙联系，适合偏好实验、前卫与当代古典的听众。独立自发行，无主流厂牌商业化倾向，整体风格独特且具有较强的艺术完整性。

items.body: Review by siLLy puPPy — While the Rock Andaluz scene was hitting Spain full force by the mid-1970s, another daring group ofbold prog enthusiasts were also offering new strains of flamenco infused jazz fusion with the lion'sshare emerging from the Catalonian city of Barcelona. While Iceberg may be the best known of thesecrafty weavers of complexity, other acts such as Companyia El�ctrica Dharma, Orquestra Mirasol,Barcelona Traction and Secta S�nica were delivering their own wild fusion expressions. Add to thatanother band M�SICA URBANA which dropped two highly revered albums in its three year existence. Thisband was perhaps the most adventurous of the lot as it tackled not only a wide swath of fusionstyles laid down by the likes of Return To Forever, Mahavishnu Orchestra, Herbie Hancock and WeatherReport but also incorporated the crafty complexities of England's Canterbury scene and if thatwasn't enough wove intricate third stream classical elements as well as the homegrown folk flavorsof the region including the sounds of Andalusian flamenco.Some of the best musicians on the scene in this one included Joan Albert Amarg�s (keyboards, windinstruments), Carles Benavent (bass, later of Paco de Luc�a's band), Salvador Font (percussion),Llu�s Cabanach (guitars), and special guest Aurora Amarg�s (castanets). The band released itseponymously titled debut in 1976 and has been considered one of the highlights of Spain's entirefusion scene from the 1970s. The band was sort of a supergroup in a local sense and very much soundslike one at this point by delivering amazingly dexterous labyrinthine compositions that intricatelyintegrated jazz, progressive rock, classical music and traditional Spanish folk musical styles withthe intent of exuding a truly Iberian vibe without sounding derivative. Perhaps comparable only toArgentina's Alas as far as unbridled complexities are concerned, M�SICA URBANA delivered anunpredictable pastiche of musical ingenuity that few acts would dare attempt much less pull off withsuch ease and grace.The album wastes no time bedazzling the unsuspecting listener with its opening "Agost" with wilycurveball guitar riffs in cahoots with slinking keyboards slithering around in strange ways whilethe bombastic incessant shifts of tempos, time signatures and dynamics prove to be a difficult taskin keeping track of. In fact it's the equivalent to a musical roller coaster that does all thoseimpossibly crazy loops and hairpin turns into the unknown. It's a wild ride that rarely allowsmoments of respite however in the middle of the turbulent fusion-fests also exist moments of melodicmellowness however they usually don't last too long before explosive bursts of energetic excesspunctuate the serenity. It's a jittery beast of an album bar none which will surely alienate all butthe most hardened fusionists looking for the absolute pinnacle of no [%*!#]s to give fusion at itsmost unapologetically dynamically creative fortified with as many high octane ingredients aspossible. It's an exhilarating ride which provides both smatterings of melodic accessibility in themidst of impossible mangled motifs of madness.While many fusionists were adopting funk about this time to ease the pain of the wild torrents ofjazz infused curveballs, M�SICA URBANA took the opposite approach and indulged in a musical free-for-all where no limits were set however the band remains firmly in the world of jazz fusion as itsprimary modus operandi. The band would calm things down a bit for its second and final releasehaving realized that perhaps there weren't enough music nerds out there to sustain the marketabilityof an album like this debut however for those of you who resemble those remarks this is an amazinglybrilliant display of jazz fusion run amok. Spain was late to the game in regard to the most daringexpressions of prog and fusion due to political repression but once the flood gates were open thisfeisty nation proved it had the talent to compete with the best on the international scene andM�SICA URBANA stands as one of Spain's most exciting and enigmatic examples.
items._cn_summary: 西班牙巴塞罗那1976年发行的Jazz Rock/Fusion专辑，融合了爵士、前卫摇滚、古典第三streams以及安达卢西亚弗拉门戈民间音乐元素。专辑以频繁的节奏变换、复杂的时间签名和强烈的动态对比著称，编曲 labyrinthine且充满冒险精神。作为西班牙70年代融合音乐场景的重要作品，其将伊比利亚半岛民间音色与欧美爵士摇滚及坎特伯雷复杂编曲手法相结合的方式，展现了独特的跨文化视野。音乐在狂暴的不规则段落与抒情段落之间快速切换，对听众的注意力提出较高要求。该专辑代表了非英语音乐地区融合实验的杰出成就。

items.body: rust/wave, his latest, takes a different approach. The Hamilton, Ontario-based artist has compiled a beautiful piece of ambient work, and rather than introducing itself as some ambient drone or sounding like that, it’s actually really melodic and beautiful. A peaceful listen. Electroacoustic composition with a raw and emotional approach rust/wave by Tewksbury   Tewksbury’s previous albums required commitment. His 2024 release Floes: Volumes I-IV was over three hours of glacial ambient music, with individual tracks stretching past 10 minutes. Brutes (2022) featured two 20-minute compositions built from 60-foot tape loops and public domain choral music. rust/wave, his latest, takes a different approach. The Hamilton, Ontario-based artist has compiled a beautiful piece of ambient work, and rather than introducing itself as some ambient drone or sounding like that, it’s actually really melodic and beautiful. A peaceful listen. Built primarily using vintage hardware samplers: the Akai Riff-o-matic, a lo-fi guitar trainer, and Korg MS-1—rust/wave embraces the imperfections and limitations of outdated technology through blown-out analog textures, lo-fi sampling, distortion, and saturated ambient processing. Doug Tewksbury has always prioritized analogue sounds in his work, but rust/wave marks a shift from the long-form, glacial pieces of Floes and Brutes toward a collection of relatively short tracks. Each piece here is concise, focused, and intentional. The album moves between ambient, experimental, and electroacoustic composition with a raw and emotional approach, influenced by artists like Burial, Portishead, Can, and Oneohtrix Point Never. “Tape warble, digital aliasing, and distortion aren’t flaws to be corrected; they’re textures to be explored.” ~ J Batista Favorites include “Rime”, with its unique pads and atmosphere that is mysterious and haunting like fading thoughts, and “Corridors,” a soft piano piece with minimal reverb applied but beautiful in its presentation. Tewksbury does this well with each track on the album, identifying each not as just another ambient piece but all having the same ambient aesthetic, yet different personalities with all the sound effects and touches he adds to them. The hardware samplers give the album a distinct character. The Akai Riff-o-matic, for instance, is a lo-fi guitar trainer from the early 90s that was never intended for serious music production, but its limitations, low bit-rate sampling, limited memory, and crude looping, become strengths in Tewksbury‘s hands. The imperfections of the hardware are foregrounded, not hidden. Tape warble, digital aliasing, and distortion aren’t flaws to be corrected; they’re textures to be explored. The imperfections of the hardware are foregrounded, not hidden :: “Illume” is one of those tracks that sends you floating and drifting away into a dreamland. Such beautiful melodies playing peacefully. Tewksbury has done this kind of beautiful peacefulness before, Paths and Floes both had moments of quiet, reflective beauty, but rust/wave feels more immediate, more accessible. The long-form works on Floes required patience and time. They unfolded over 10+ minutes, slowly building and dissolving. rust/wave is more direct. The tracks are shorter, the melodies more pronounced, the emotional core more present. It’s hard to pull off sometimes in this type of genre, but this one is special. Ambient music has a tendency to either drift into formlessness or lean too heavily on preset patches and easy atmospheres. Tewksbury avoids both. The melodies here are strong enough to hold your attention, and the production is textured enough to reward close listening. The vintage hardware samplers give the album a tactile quality, you can hear the machinery at work, the limitations being pushed. It’s not pristine. It’s not polished. rust/wave is a reminder that imperfection can be beautiful, and that technology doesn’t need to be cutting-edge to make something worthwhile. For a label debut on Imaginary North, this is a strong entry. Tewksbury has found a sound that’s both personal and inviting, and rust/wave is proof that sometimes the best work comes from embracing limitations rather than fighting them. rust/wave is available on Imaginary North. [Bandcamp] rust/wave by Tewksbury
items._cn_summary: Tewksbury的rust/wave是一张氛围电子与实验音乐融合的作品，巧妙运用1990年代的低保真硬件采样器如Akai Riff-o-matic和Korg MS-1，将设备本身的局限性转化为独特的声音纹理。专辑放弃了他此前长篇冰川式ambient的做法，转而采用简洁的短曲目形式，在氛围、实验与电声作曲之间游走，呈现出粗粝而真挚的情感表达。受Burial、Portishead、Oneohtrix Point Never等影响，作品强调模拟质感的探索，将磁带颤音、数字失真和饱和处理作为可挖掘的音色而非需修正的缺陷。这一做法既体现了技术上的创新意识，也展现了独特的艺术视角，与用户对实验/前卫及电子音乐的偏好高度契合。

items.body: Review by Fercandio46 — I was pleasantly surprised by this Adrian Belew album, where he blends several of his various facets.A13 sounds very spontaneous; the presence of the piano reminded me of the warmth of Mr. Music Head. Belew plays all the instruments here, and that guitar, which sometimes sounds like the 60s and other times avant-garde, sometimes like King Crimson and other times like the Beatles, Elevator is a return to his song-like format, but played... well played, including virtuosic instrumental parts with a certain degree of risk.A Car I Can Talk To incorporates 50s rock and soul into the blues, with those train station sounds from his extensive repertoire, as vast as a magician's hat.In Backwards and Upside Down, he makes use of his high and low vocals, as well as his most pyrotechnic, 80s-style Crimson guitar, which, almost as if traveling the world, not just time, takes us to Japan.When Adrian Belew picks up a guitar, he can be just as devastating as with an electric one... he has already demonstrated this and does it again in The Power of the Natural World, but with variations compared to the past, with small, almost ethnic instrumental details. In Elevator, he has dressed his guitar in different outfits; it is the undisputed protagonist, along with his voice. Good Morning Sun finds novel discoveries in the editing and layering of instruments.The Saturday Morning Roar revisits the experiments with electronic music, where the backing tracks, along with his guitar improvising synthesized solos, reach one of the album's greatest peaks. When only the piano remains, it takes on a different meaning. Many colors...many facets...many sounds...many overlapping layers make up a fun Belew.Attitude interweaves keyboard arrangements with intricate guitar scales that allow for layering.Taking My Shoes Out for a Walk features more textures...acoustic guitars and spoken word over aggressive sections reminiscent of the Henry Rollins Band.At times, it sounds like Allan Holdsworth, a style that continues in Back to Love, the album's final and most experimental section, in this almost chronological journey through influences, including volumes one, two, and three from the first decade of the 2000s.A whole sonic framework that, remaining in Fripp's band, wouldn't have allowed him to develop, and yet we find those sentimental fragments that were in King Crimson (which we know were his) in Beauty, and an ending with Seventy Going on Seventeen that reminds me a lot of early Bowie...which is very special coming from Belew...I could almost hear him singing it, and the album is completed as a synthesis that contributes meaning but with joyful passion.
items._cn_summary: Adrian Belew于2022年发行的《Elevator》是一张折衷主义浓厚的前卫摇滚专辑，展现了这位吉他手从60年代复古、80年代King Crimson风格到前卫实验的多元音乐轨迹。专辑融合了蓝调、灵魂乐、电子即兴、世界音乐元素（民族乐器细节与日本音乐意象），通过钢琴、合成器与层次丰富的吉他编排交织出独特的声场。Belew的多面演奏能力在这张自弹自唱的个人专辑中发挥得淋漓尽致，既有情感化的抒情段落，也有高风险的技术性器乐段落。评论详细描述了音乐的多维层次和艺术深度，对于关注实验与前卫音乐的用户而言，这张兼具创新性与个人风格的作品具有较高的参考价值。

items.body: Review by Fercandio46 — The third and final part of Gong's Radio Gnome Invisible trilogy, where Zero, the hero, receives his cosmic ascension, activating his third eye...deserved an imposing musical framework, befitting the importance of the events narrated. This volume thus became the most musically daring, the most experimental, and the one with the longest tracks. While each part was unique in its own way...and Angel's Egg had innovated with the short duration of its tracks and yet all its stylistic variety, You further developed these concepts, taking them a step further and becoming a classic not only for the band but for the genre itself.As the cover promises...there's a mix of spacey atmosphere and indigenous mysticism in Thoughts for Naught, Daevid Allen's composition, his ability to draw the rest into his universe...Tim Blake's synthesizers and Mike Howlett's bass in Magick Mother Invocation, creating that spacey psychedelia that always starts slowly...Didier Malherbe's saxophone, Gilli Smyth's vocals, and of course Pierre and Beno�t Moerlen's drums and percussion...plus Steve Hillage's ineffable and unmistakable guitar...everything will conspire to make that conjunction of stars explode in this volume.Master Builder is the construction of that curtain of synthesizers and the Buddhist choir...the percussion, the flute in an oriental orchestra...until the drums introduce the saxophone and the space rock jam...the cosmic French psychedelic free jazz begins...you can smell the 70s...you can feel it...there is precision, there is technique...yes...but there is also madness, freedom, anarchy, bohemianism, and that mix is ​​what made this Gong so special, ultimately, Allen's invocatory presence. When Hillage begins to play...nobody was prepared for that cascade of sound...for those doors that open in the mind with the notes of his sound...which, supported by the synthesizer, the drums and the bass, will make history.You is an album that wasn't rushed...in a decade that seized control of time to do with it as it saw fit for artistic purposes...and if this meant accelerating it to the point of confusion like King Crimson on Red...or slowing it down to the point of despair...like Gentle Giant on Free Hand...there was no doubt they were going to do it, and Gong took the time to build each step of ascent on You...because they knew that the feeling of climbing step by step is not the same as skipping steps in pursuit of a rush that only speaks of detachment from things.As layers of synthesizers build upon the drums in A Sprinkling of Clouds, and the drums with each hit seem to leap from the speakers and reach us as only a few records can...and the guitar sounds wild yet clean at the same time and you can follow its path at every moment...when Didier Malherbe joins in we understand why they distanced themselves from anyone who could do something similar and Frank Zappa's Inca's Roads didn't end up going in the same direction either.Perfect Mystery revisits the cabaret atmosphere of Angel's Egg only as a connection within the story, that oriental atmosphere that sets the stage for The Isle of Everywhere, one of the album's central themes...where synthesizers, Gilli Smyth's vocals, bass, and drums create an atmosphere reminiscent of King Crimson's Islands...only to then turn around and take another route, because Mike Howlett's swing on the bass had the necessary propulsion to soar without sopranos...and Gong sometimes has the ability to pass the third eye to us, if we can connect with his music; it's jazz...it's progressive rock...it's funk...it's psychedelia...it's the Canterbury scene, born in part because an Australian couldn't return to England and had to stay in France.Steve Hillage's solo begins so subtly behind the saxophone...but it does define itself throughout the entire development, supported by the bass and drums, at times playing with parts of jazz rock, until You Never Blow Your Trip Forever encompasses everything heard so far in the trilogy, even more psychedelic if possible...until it settles as if unintentionally into a section that, from improvised and played, culminates in another inspired song/prayer to the universe...a mantra repeated and destined to fade away, the complete opposite of this third volume of the most classic Gong which, as if it were a loop in time...must be repeated again and again once it has already ended.
items._cn_summary: GONG乐队的《You》是1974年Canterbury Scene与太空摇滚融合的里程碑作品，作为Radio Gnome Invisible三部曲的终章，专辑在音乐上极具冒险精神。专辑融合了合成器音效、自由爵士萨克斯、即兴演奏与东方神秘主义元素，构建出层次丰富的声响景观。Steve Hillage的吉他演奏、Tim Blake的合成器实验与Didier Malherbe的爵士萨克斯风段落交织，配合佛教合唱与打击乐的编排，呈现出跨越类型边界的实验性架构。专辑中的长篇幅曲目展现了乐队在即兴与结构之间的平衡能力，以及对声音空间感的精准把控。这张专辑以其跨领域融合特质与创新的音乐语言，契合了实验/前卫音乐爱好者的聆听期待。

items.body: Dikke tien jaar na zijn eerste soloalbum (“Filth Haven” op Malignant Records , 2015) keert de experimentele muzikant en sounddesigner Kristoffer Oustad uit het Noorse Arendal terug met "Magnor", deze keer op het Poolse Zoharum label.   Kristoffer Oustad heeft al een gevarieerde muzikale carrière achter de rug, beginnend met extreme metal in de black/death/industrial metal projecten V:O:I:D en V:28 , voordat hij zich meer op experimentele muziek en sounddesign begon te richten. “Magnor” (7 tracks, 45 minuten speelduur) klinkt als een filmische, gelaagde en ijzige ontdekkingsreis door dark ambient en industriële muziek. Het album zit geworteld in klassieke industrial- en dark ambient-tradities (vooral de typisch Scandinavische), maar met een zeer persoonlijke benadering. De kern van het album is het thema van spirituele verbondenheid of een kompas in de leegte. Het album nodigt je expliciet uit om die ijzige leegte te betreden, met de muziek zelf als je enige kompas. De albumtitel is ontleend aan een Noors grensplaatsje. Voor Oustad is Magnor niet zomaar een geografische locatie. Het staat symbool voor een fysieke plek, een richting én een specifieke gemoedstoestand. De muziek onderzoekt de intense relatie tussen Oustad en de ruwe, onherbergzame Scandinavische natuur die zijn identiteit vormt. Het album ademt een sfeer van eenzaamheid, nostalgie en geografische isolatie. "Magnor" is gecomponeerd en gerijpt over meerdere jaren, met behulp van analoge en modulaire synthesizers, minimale nabewerking en een sterke focus op structuur, dynamiek en sfeer, met zeer weinig digitale opsmuk achteraf. De muziek werd live ingespeeld, eerder dan strak voorgeprogrammeerd, wat het een gevoel van aanwezigheid en authenticiteit verleent en een cruciaal onderdeel vormt van het karakter van het album. Voor het album maakte Oustad intensief gebruik van analoge effecten, diepe drones en korrelige ruis. “Magnor” vraagt om geduld van de luisteraar, maar beloont die met een diepe en meeslepende luisterervaring. De nummers ademen een ijzige, desolate Scandinavische sfeer en doen zeer filmisch aan.  “White Sacred Arrow” zet als openingsnummer direct de toon en is met een lengte van bijna tien minuten de langste compositie op het album. Het nummer fungeert als de poort naar de ijzige, desolate wereld van “Magnor”. Het is de kompasnaald die naar het Noorden wijst. Het begint extreem minimalistisch met diepe, pulserende bassen, die aanvoelen als een gure wind over een desolaat Noors landschap. Oustad dwingt de luisteraar tot geduld. Pas na enkele minuten transformeren de minimale drones zich via analoge synthesizers in een zware, tastbare muur van geluid en subtiele melodie. Het weerspiegelt perfect het centrale albumthema van een spirituele zoektocht of een kompas in de leegte. Mijn favoriet en de absolute uitschieter van het album is ongetwijfeld de tweede track “The Beacon”, met quasi continu gekraak over de enigmatische, dreigende en stikdonkere ambient klanken. Het nummer vormt een direct, logisch vervolg op de ijzige openingstrack. Het brengt een subtiele verschuiving in de dynamiek van het album en fungeert als een baken (beacon) in de leegte: De titel sluit naadloos aan bij het centrale albumthema van een spirituele zoektocht en de metafoor van het album als een kompas in de duisternis en leegte. Waar de eerste track je achterlaat in een desolaat, ijskoud landschap, fungeert dit nummer als een sonisch lichtpunt of oriëntatiepunt waar de luisteraar naartoe wordt getrokken. Ook hier wordt gebruik gemaakt van modulaire synthesizers. Het nummer drijft op langgerekte, diepe analoge drones die gestaag pulseren. In plaats van een abrupte climax te zoeken, blijft het nummer hangen in een constante, hypnotiserende staat van spanning. De overgang vanuit de ijzige rust van de eerste track naar de meer abstracte, minimalistische geluidsstructuren van de volgende tracks (zoals “A Consequence Of Entropy”, “Bring Back The Wolves” en “The Gravity Of Colour”) wordt hiermee perfect ingezet. "A Consequence Of Entropy": entropie – zo weten we nog uit de lessen fysica en thermodynamica - staat voor chaos en het langzaam vervallen van systemen. Dit sluit aan bij de melancholie van een verlaten grensstreek waar de tijd lijkt stil te staan en de natuur de menselijke sporen langzaam terugwint. Het nummer "Bring Back The Wolves", de middelste track, de vierde van zeven, kan gezien worden als het absolute, angstaanjagende hoogtepunt en de muzikale climax van de plaat. Het roept het ruwe, gevaarlijke en pure Scandinavische verleden op. Het staat symbool voor het terugkeren naar de basis en de herintroductie van de wilde natuur in de leegte. In “The Gravity Of Colour”, de vijfde track,  zit een dialoog tussen een man en een vrouw. “The Gravity Of Color” hint naar hoe zwaar de grauwe, monochrome kleuren van het Noorse winterlandschap op de menselijke psyche kunnen drukken, zoals een winterdepressie in de lange poolnacht.  “Magnetic Blood” vormt als voorlaatste nummer de opmaat naar de ontknoping (“Detachment”). De titel verraadt het al: het nummer heeft een ‘magnetische’, dwingende, hypnotiserende aantrekkingskracht. Je hoort hier weer duidelijk de live ingespeelde, modulaire synthesizers. Er zit een constante, onderhuidse spanning en ritmische puls in die doet denken aan een kloppende hartslag of stromend bloed door de aderen. "Magnetic Blood" is qua songtitel de meest directe verwijzing naar de onlosmakelijke, spirituele binding met een plek. De aantrekkingskracht van de Heimat zit de artiest letterlijk in het bloed, alsof een intern kompas hem er altijd naar terugtrekt. "Detachment" vormt de absolute, conceptuele ontknoping van de plaat. Waar het album begint met een zoektocht, staat dit laatste nummer volledig in het teken van de betekenis van de titel: loslating en onthechting. Meest opvallend is hier het poëtische spoken word door J onathan Grieve , bekend van het Britse ambient-industrial en experimental project Contrastate . Zijn indringende spoken word, waarin de songtitel regelmatig terugkeert, snijdt diep door de muziek heen. Dit geeft het nummer een menselijke, maar tegelijkertijd spookachtige en theatrale lading. Muzikaal gezien fungeert de track als de emotionele nasleep. De dwingende, mechanische hartslag uit de voorgaande track, “Magnetic Blood”, is hier weggeëbd. Wat overblijft is een ijle, melancholische en mistige soundscape. De analoge drones zwellen nog één keer aan om een getormenteerde, desolate sfeer neer te zetten. Daarna lossen ze langzaam op in het niets. Het nummer laat de luisteraar achter met een onbehaaglijk, maar sereen gevoel van berusting. Met “Detachment” sluit Kristoffer Oustad de cirkel van zijn spirituele en muzikale kompas. De intense industriële spanning maakt definitief plaats voor pure, ijzige leegte. https://oustad.bandcamp.com Magnor by Kristoffer Oustad
items._cn_summary: 这是一张融合dark ambient、工业声响与影像化氛围的实验性专辑，来自挪威独立音乐人Kristoffer Oustad。专辑以斯堪的纳维亚荒野为主题，探讨地理孤立感与精神寻找的深层联系。音乐使用模拟合成器和模块化合成器构建深沉的 drones 与颗粒感噪声，整体以现场演奏而非程序化方式呈现，赋予作品呼吸感与真实存在感。七首曲目层层递进，开场曲《White Sacred Arrow》以极简主义手法铺展冷冽音景，《The Beacon》则以持续的低频震颤构建神秘不安的氛围。专辑强调结构与动态的精心编排，呈现克制而内敛的艺术视角，适合偏好实验暗潮与氛围声响的听者。

The first is from Perry Farrell of Jane's Addiction: "Camera got them images / Camera got them all / Nothing's shocking... " The second, often attributed to William S. items.body:
Two quotes come to mind in the wake of Simon Hanes' Gargantua. The first is from Perry Farrell of Jane's Addiction: "Camera got them images / Camera got them all / Nothing's shocking... " The second, often attributed to William S. Burroughs: "Nothing is true, everything is permitted." Taken together, they suggest a world where boundaries dissolve and meaning becomes fluid. Hanes both affirms and challenges that premise in this sprawling, provocative work.

Gargantua is written for an unconventional large ensemble: three drum kits, three electric basses, three trombones, three French horns, and three voices. The sheer scale of the instrumentation hints at excess, but the result is far from chaotic. Hanes, an acolyte of downtown icon John Zorn, has built a reputation for stylistic range, composing for his Italian soundtrack—inspired ensemble Tredici Bacci, the experimental surf project Tsons of Tsunami, the thrash/improv outfit Trigger, and a variety of contemporary classical contexts. Here, he brings those disparate threads into a single, ambitious statement.

The music operates like an intricate collage; layered, deliberate and densely referential. Hanes draws inspiration from a journey through Norway, the volcanic force of Iceland and Hawaii, and François Rabelais's 16th-century epic Gargantua and Pantagruel, a once-scandalous satire of giants and excess. To this he adds fragments of Buddhist texts, passages from Dante's Inferno, baroque gestures, minimalist repetition and the raw energy of rock and metal. On paper, the combination seems unwieldy; in practice, it recalls the eclectic logic of Frank Zappa's ensembles or Zorn's Naked City band, where unlikely elements cohere through force of vision.

Across the album's ten tracks, there are no featured soloists. The emphasis is squarely on composition and collective execution. The fifteen musicians function as a single, shifting organism, navigating Hanes' abrupt transitions and layered structures. The journey is global and temporal: ancient philosophies collide with modern noise, sacred texts meet irreverent outbursts. "Submit to the Fabulosity," for instance, blends disco-inflected rhythms with percussive density, while its vocalists deliver a barrage of profane invective. Elsewhere, "Moirai" offers a moment of fragile, almost sacred vocal harmony, only to be shattered by the abrasive intensity of "Lacerated by a Flying Shard."

Hanes moves freely between extremes, baroque intricacy and heavy-metal force, serene minimalism and explosive noise, linking Stravinsky to Led Zeppelin, alpine folk traditions to contemporary experimentalism. The result is music that feels both overwhelming and meticulously constructed, a constant oscillation between order and rupture.

Gargantua is not an easy listen, nor is it meant to be. It is a demanding, immersive work that unfolds more fully with repeated exposure. What initially registers as excess reveals itself, over time, as a carefully shaped landscape of contrasts. In the end, Hanes doesn't simply argue that "nothing is shocking," he suggests that meaning still emerges from the collision of ideas, that even in a world without clear boundaries, form and purpose can be forged.
items._cn_summary: Simon Hanes的《Gargantua》是一张为大编制非常规乐团（三个鼓组、低音提琴、长号、法国号和人声各三件）创作的实验性作品，承袭John Zorn的纽约下城美学传统。专辑以拼贴手法融合巴洛克繁复、极简主义重复、重金属能量与古代哲学文本，呈现出跨越时空与文化边界的音响景观。十五位乐手以集体演出为核心，无独奏家主导，所有注意力集中于作曲结构与整体呈现。专辑在平静的人声和声与尖锐的噪音爆发之间剧烈摆荡，展示了Hanes将看似矛盾的元素凝聚为统一音乐话语的能力。整张专辑要求听众的持续参与，初听可能显得冗余，但重复聆听后会揭示出精心构建的音响层次与叙事逻辑。对于偏好实验、前卫与学院派爵士融合的听者而言，这是一部值得深入探索的作品。

items.excerpt: soak vol 2 unfolds like a damaged transmission from somewhere intimate and unplaceable—32 fractured, emotional, and strangely beautiful pieces stitched together from the outer edges of contemporary electronic sound. An international community focused on contemporary sound soak vol 2 by soak   Angular and granular electronica with some minor guitarica. There is probably no dancing and definitely no sleeping, this is all art—so rejoice! 32 very strange episodes, plenty to baffle the listener.
items.body: soak vol 2 unfolds like a damaged transmission from somewhere intimate and unplaceable—32 fractured, emotional, and strangely beautiful pieces stitched together from the outer edges of contemporary electronic sound. An international community focused on contemporary sound soak vol 2 by soak   Angular and granular electronica with some minor guitarica. There is probably no dancing and definitely no sleeping, this is all art—so rejoice! 32 very strange episodes, plenty to baffle the listener. Soak (the record label) is based in Petropavl, Kazakhstan. Soak 2 is a second compilation album by that label, an international community focused on contemporary sound as a means of emotional liberation & self-inquiry, featuring various kinds of music, ranging from lamebient & downtempo to quirky sound-design, raw sonic intimacy & processed emo, whatever that may be. “This is something we are proud to share, aiming at fostering a sense of unity, artistic freedom & love.“ The project was gathered and meticulously curated throughout 2025. “We hadn’t planned it to turn out that long, 32 tracks crept up like an uncontrolled desire of getting tattooed over and over again. As a result, ‘soak body’ is etched with a (s)extensive selection of self-recognition-evoking music by sound producers & musicians across the globe. Raw or refined, recorded live, carefully produced, (un)processed or playfully generated, the diversity of sound and approach eventually point at something intimate: the ‘how to be’. A shared ‘something’ we truly celebrate together via media at hand.”​ A part of proceeds will go to Isaakov dog shelter in Petropavl, Kazakhstan. The artists heard on this anthology are: s[].any, goo, lycopsid_,  OL,  sidechain unit, tumy, free version, other joe, louis vogue,  яома bantik ³³³,  obe,  s.drift,  double blind,  Alien Recycling,  obi uto,  moemu, zuno,  Infant,  Kilou,  virtual echo,  DJ Birdbath,  kk.Shucko,  marat koshkin,  Yerofeyev,  16:9 ratio,  duun,  ebilen, inferior design,  Alien Team,  slyn, poole,  bad lsd trips,  defkon, and Sta Dormida. Curated by a b, marat koshkin & a. doina, Mostly mastered by yeyo & a b. Artwork by marat koshkin & a. doina. Merch design by marat koshkin. One of the best aspects of anthologies is that smaller projects have the opportunity to exhibit in a common showcase, reaching more of the whole community, to expose their work and to experience the reactions. None of the tracks are very long, the shortest one is less than one minute. If something puts you off, hang on, there will be something new coming along soon, or maybe more of the same but somehow different. Some aspects are similar, but each track stands alone. The names are creative, to decode this, here you will find the moniker of the creating entity, a hyphen, followed by the track title and the length in minutes, and a brief description of what I think that I heard. 1. s[].any – t.here 05:55 — Opens into a dark mood, I imagine that I hear many voices hidden in the mix, which is a sound collage, with different surprises. Our dreamy poetic singer is honest, the overall sound has lots of little flavors in a delicious complex collage stew. So strange. 2. goo – Secret 03:37 — A classical guitar, with some electronics whirled about, a cello, a singer, a robot plumber. Fragments of voices that echo amidst the tunneling strings and things. Easy drifting instrumentals with strange effects and odd bits here and there. 3. lycopsid_ – raupe 03:40 — “Lycopsid” is a botanical term for clubmosses, and Lycopsid (or lycopsid) is a Leipzig, Germany-based musical artist, known for producing electronic or ambient music, with tracks available on platforms like Bandcamp and Pandora. The sound here is celestial, a steady awakening into increasing brightness with interesting sound collages or wet chattering bits sprinkled and patterned about. 4. OL – Softshell 02:08 — The collected cadence is a bit loose, mumbling taps and tings, shuffling percussive snaps and shudders. It lunges forward, it pauses and holds, it shifts and prepares to lunge, it starts again. I can dig it. It whispers to me about beats while staying fluid and just flowing with sticky stop-start moments built in. 5. sidechain unit – wasted youth riddim 03:32 — I think there are voices, fragments including screaming happy kids in a playground hidden within the mix, which comes up harsh and stays very interesting, percussive clacks, perhaps some island riddim, there are ghosts flicker dancing, and a roller coaster where they all scream together. The beat is skeletal, with an odd missing beat pattern and new mumbling taps and tings, shuffling percussive snaps and shudders. 6. tumy – frostlings 03:48 — A dusty ghost piano melody loop and an agitated electronic spirit bouncing about, echo effects gone wild, in a deep dub style. There are many things going on at once, the piano, and percussive elements that echo and shatter, about half way through the strange beat gets stronger. The piano stays perfectly on course. 7. free version – moonlight yuh spotlight yuh 06:05 — Somewhere in the abandoned old factory ruins by the sea, in a big dark cave there are strange radios playing, or maybe poetic people reciting lines, or both and more. This sounds like it is probably dangerous, voices are talking and there are echoes, plenty of water. I do not understand any words, which are mostly repetitive. There are large monsters moving about off in the distance, I hear some smoothly running machine noises and banging about. And more water. 8. other joe – every image (ft. concave reflection) 04:28 — A piano, people breathing, someone is talking, there is some kind of electronic instrument, nice and slow. Mystery at every moment, dripping water, maybe a flute, odd woodwinds, slow and quiet and cautious, full of microscopic details. Spraying water? The piano keeps dreaming and seems distant sometimes. The bowed drones have the sky here. 9. louis vogue – out of reach (ft. saga charlotte) 00:59 — Louis Vogue is an electronic music artist, DJ, and co-founder of the Brussels-based collective and event series Club Détour, known for playing atmospheric and experimental sets on Kiosk Radio. The short dreamy misty track bursts in, I hear drama, sadness and darkness on a sweeping scale, singing over the storm of glitchy-pitched musical tones. 10. яома bantik ³³³ – ₉⁹₉ (yeyo & a b edit) 02:16 — ЯOMA BANTIK @romabantik is a Russian artist from the Urals, working with metal, natural and industrial heritages. I hear a fella and his guitar, strummin’ and singin’, sounds great to me. Good times, with no serious fancy science fiction studio effects. A young man alone, telling his heart. 11. obe – iji’s dub 06:37 — I think this one feels like we are deep underwater, the throbbing reverb feels like a dub mix, with various bouncing pulse echoes, the playful living echo vibration creature crawls about above the constant pulse flowing inward slowly then flowing outward, repeating, like breathing in your sleep. The dark water flows for miles below us. There are UFOs down there too. 12. s.drift – quatro CD 03:50 — Nervous  and clicky like a rhythm, or maybe more like a collage, with odd forward and backward sounds, blending into a lighter abstract clicky beat, maybe adding a hi hat cymbal effect, an unexpected voice beep pops by a few times, while the shadows shake and shimmy. A drum set somehow shows up. We step forth with pep. 13. double blind – fade 02:29 — Water flowing, strange environmental humming rings, with mysterious winds and rain. The voice sounds drained and perhaps coming from another world. The message is in the form of hopeful poetry, and is not obvious. In my mind’s eye I see candles in the misty rings. 14. Alien Recycling – Pareidolia Cat Dub 03:44 — I am always trying to find meaningful faces or messages in musical clouds or in chaos. Here is an electronic cat that slides. There is an echo rhythm beat, drawing some space night ramblers. The beat is not steady and nearly seems to fall apart, and rallies a few times then eases off. I have been feeding that cat. 15. obi uto – oysq 03:33 — Perhaps this is just how they talk, strange beeps and clicking-rushing tones. No beats, no words, plenty of odd looping collage fragmentations, pulling from a unique musique concrete style and beyond. The feeling is restless. 16. moemu, zuno – petal traces 04:47 — Moemu and zuno are two musical artists associated with ambient, electronic, chill-out music contexts or lo-fi soundscapes, often featured in mix sets, and are found on Pandora and Bandcamp. I hear fragments of so many things, dark loop dreams that make no sense but are restful, pouring spilling cascading repeating flowing falling scattering evaporating, restless and gently convulsive, chaotic, there are void ghosts and melancholia floods over the roller coasters. I try to get there early and stay late. 17. Infant – jewel 03:01 — From twitchy robot bleeps to greebles rumbling, coming through a small tube with some shortwave radio throbbing and ringing, or maybe they are simply talking amongst themselves. There are  little spinning bumping bells and a tap-ring collage. A beat comes about, explodes and gets wild, smooths and bumps along, the flow always gets busy in places after the extended coasting interludes. soak vol 2 by Kilou   18. Kilou – Blurry 03:40 — Somewhere deep in space we float upside down, feet over eyebrows, there is buzzing and a musical instrument strumming lightly. Some guy is singing while the dragons and other monsters size the room. Soon chains are broken. A guy is talking and singing, playing a guitar, flying feathered electronic snakes swirling about, seeking a hole in outer space. I hear strumming, spare shovels and  tapping glasses with ice. I didn’t tell you everything. 19. virtual echo – j trip 04:35 — In the wash water, jiggling as the machine works, the sloshing water sets the beat. I hear nifty chattering little rhythms and throbbing waves of activities, her voices echo, skyrockets splash, there may be a drum kit, and now we are cooking, throbbing right along. This is where I belong. 20. DJ Birdbath – Rose Drip 04:06 — DJ Birdbath is the artist name for Ian Baxter, an electronic music producer based in the South Island of New Zealand, known for ambient and experimental music, often featuring deconstructed sounds, fragmented rhythms, and shoegaze-tinged vocals influenced by his past, often using a mix of real and generated samples. His music is featured on NTS Radio, SoundCloud, and Bandcamp. He released the album Memory Empathy (2024) via Theory Therapy, which features a blend of samples and influences from his time in the UK. The sound here is an abstract beat pattern that never stops changing, loops with flowing chaos and surprises, mostly variations on the instrumental constructions. Somewhere about half way in, they settle into a very catchy complex groove that stays uncertain but keeps going. They fly off, they fade. 21. kk.Shucko – another missed mirage 03:26 — kk.Shucko is an San Francisco-based experimental club producer and DJ known for crafting intricate, high-res techno, IDM, and warped drum and bass soundscapes, her sets revel in composing evenings that sew together soft and hard, continuity and catharsis draw listeners into an alien realm, and fuses needy rhythms, ambient, and club music to create immersive, imagined biomes. Associated with Club Moniker and Ommaya Records, they create “hyperspace” audio, often incorporating elements like glass and gel, and hold a residency at SutroFM. I hear energized chattering electronic squirrels, also scratchy electronified voices painted on the air. The squirrels keep me busy, some of the sound is harsh with whispers hidden inside, hit with sharp short and zappy bolts, melting into a bubbling sea of writhing monsters and phantoms. Darned cool. 22. marat koshkin – cry OS 03:37 — Marat Koshkin is a musician and artist from Petropavlovsk, Kazakhstan, recently located in Saint-Petersburg. The beat is catchy from the jump, splashy weaving beats stay strong and powerful mixed with the collage nicely, gettin’ jammy with multiple instruments, gettin’ down within the change and solids. A winsome laugh has been captured. 23. Yerofeyev – Smares (Senglar Rmx) 05:52 — Senglar is an electronic music artist and composer known for producing experimental, atmospheric, immersive, often dark, and downtempo electronic soundscapes. Based on recent music releases, Senglar often works within the niche of electronic, ambient, and downtempo genres, featuring 2024 album releases like Sensen – Hum. A rolling ball of fragmented multisounds, shortwave abstract whispers, electronic complex and plenty to listen to per sparkle, great for head rushes and surprises. I am sure there is more to the story as to how Senglar came to remix Yerofeyev’s Smares. 24. 16:9 ratio – Nothing Drive 03:15 — 16:9 ratio is likely the moniker for Geunf, a multidisciplinary artist, DJ, and producer based in Ottawa, Canada. He is known for blending techno, pop, and deconstructed club music. He released the ambient/experimental project Our Keyboards in 2025. He is also a member of the pop trio Los3r. I hear a children’s playground and people talking just out of reach, the beat trots up and off we go with nice propulsion, dancing snowflakes, the feeling defines royal and grand (both), towards the end we are at a full gallop with happily laughing snare drums and a big wow finish. 25. duun – chill! 03:28 — A machine is dancing inside of a twisting huge towering steel monster, I sense a dark voodoo beach with a moonlight fire, the rolling beat goes on and on, the feeling is fearsome and close, I hear a sly dark dub beat, probably from a strong dancing doom machine. 26. ebilen – aeon 04:00 — Ebilen is an electronic music artist known for tracks like “Strange Emotion” and the album pihkal (Base 1), releasing music through labels like Tabula Rasa Records and featuring on SoundCloud. They produce in genres often associated with underground electronic or ambient styles. I am in outer space, no gravity, no up or down, spinning slowly, whispers always getting more complex, shifting and ticking inside the mind. Something changes, the energizing chaos dance continues while ghosts call in the dark empty corridors, tiny punchy robot construction workers appear everywhere all at once for a little while, things continue to change, finally we finish swirling with whispers and the clock ticks. 27. inferior design – conning 04:47 — Outer space has no corners or answers, aliens and robots scoot along as we explore all these little pieces, like sand only smaller and with more shapes and colors, flashing and glittering particles spreading everywhere. There is no gravity so the spinning can seem slower, granular overstimulation transports some to a new place with new possibilities. Now we are having a sunrise inside the chaos collage, shooting lasers across the tracks, as chaos echoes and bumps about. This too shall morph. 28. Alien Team – my team 03:33 — Somewhere way out there, by a waterfall, the birdbeams call as they rush by. The rumbling loop brings up the low end, the birdbeams come and go, now we have a beat rumble stomp shake throbstep march while the birdbeams swirl overhead. A continuation of rushing water, with new strange birds taking over and proliferating, growing and developing, learning to dance. Soon the tribe is grooving. Now we are at the waterfall with the chaos birds. I woke up wondering where I was. At home of course. 29. slyn, poole – arc 04:18 — Slyn, a Glasgow-based sound artist, live performer, and DJ, is known for immersive, experimental, and eccentric club sounds that blend IDM, bass, and jungle with ambient textures, heavily influenced by a background in marine biology and themes of hydrofeminism and queer ecology, with soundscapes that are often described as underwater, dreamy, or “algae-like.” I am seeking more about Poole. What I hear here is a new jungle of fabrics and textures, mysterious vocalisms, many things at once. There is a primitive beat picking up, I hear the jungle in the distance. Now and then some guitar tapping time baps along. I want to live here under the arc. 30. bad lsd trips – eno river 04:46 — bad lsd trips is a collaborative music project between artists Domingo Castillo Flores and Mónica Mesa (who performs as doris dana). Based in Miami, Florida, the duo formed during the pandemic, producing music that blends elements of early industrial, dark ambient, tape music, and drone “psychedelic meditations” and “murky field recordings” with “ASMR-adjacent synths.” My mind melts, I hear strange twisted whistles, an emerging beat like a train rattle power turnip ringing shards of metal along comes the boat, an odd motor throb whispering starshine flotters about and the motor keeps running. The individual words are lost for me, the poetic tone and vibe are clear and strong, I float off into another dream with newer words that are never easier to remember. 31. defkon – sun tunnels 03:04 — We are building a new solar passageway, and adding a piano loop skeleton with strange attachments and things to tap. The piano stays solid while the changes bring new creatures that make sound, odd new sounds, piano loops and wild improv with little hand instruments adding into the pattern. 32. Sta Dormida – Trace Abruption 04:44 — Sta Dormida is an independent musical artist, singer-songwriter, producer, and audio engineer who composes, records, produces, mixes, and masters their own music. Known for releases such as Ace of Grace (2025), More Like Never (2025), and It’s Rigged (2024), they are active on platforms like Spotify and Bandcamp. This contribution features her singing and playing classical guitar, nothing electronic, just dry fingers on strings and layered singing. I want to stay here forever. Soak 2 is the second anthology, the first anthology is titled Soak, or soak, and was released on January 24, 2025.The soak music label is an international community focused on contemporary sound as a means of emotional liberation & self-inquiry.Soak (volume 1) features Geklaper, state of radiance, jerom, yeyo, d. towärds, AL-90, Monokle, ihatejulyyy, a b, saga charlotte, margaritki, sonoj, dovecot, yusk, wardi, monocoat, hiromu, secret getii, Igor Dyachenko, qwqwqwqwa, emre girginkaya, philip cock, marat koshkin, doris dana, Morning Sex, and Mélodie Blaison.This annual anthology project has a logo, “the design traces the legacy of Maud Wagner, reimagined in a state of petrified transmutation where tattoos appear as carved scars.”Maud Wagner (1877–1961) was a fearless figure who utilized her skills and unique appearance to gain financial independence and influence in a largely hidden subculture, and left a lasting legacy as the first known female tattoo artist in the United States. A former circus aerialist, she pioneered the male-dominated industry in the early 1900s by mastering traditional hand-poked (“stick-and-poke”) tattooing, helping to introduce tattoo artistry to inland America. soak vol 2 is available on soak. items._cn_summary: soak vol 2是一张来自哈萨克斯坦Petropavl的独立厂牌Soak策划的国际合辑，收录32首碎片化、情感丰富且风格各异的实验电子曲目。专辑以棱角分明、颗粒化的电子声响为核心，融合环境氛围、低保真音色与实验性声音设计，展现了当代边缘电子音乐的多样面貌。全球各地的声音制作人参与其中，曲目时长普遍极短，强调瞬间的声音冲击与情绪传递。作为一份艺术导向的独立发行，专辑体现了对情感解放与自我探索的关注，其非商业性质与来自中亚地区的独特视角为其增添了额外的文化价值。对于偏好实验与前卫音乐的听众而言，这是一张能够拓展听觉边界、发现新声音的合辑。

items.body: Review by A Crimson Mellotron — Explorers Club is one of the most exciting prog supergroups of the 90s. This Magna Carta project isheaded and masterminded by Trent Gardner, keyboard player and songwriter for Magellan, who is herejoined by John Petrucci on guitars, Billy Sheehan on bass guitar, and Terry Bozzio on drums,together with four different vocalists, among which the names of James LaBrie and D. C. Cooper makea serious impression. Additionally, the supergroup's debut album features contributions from DerekSherinian (keyboards), Wayne Gardner (guitars), Steve Howe (acoustic guitar), and James Murphy(guitars). Composed by Trent Gardner, 'Age of Impact', as goes the title of this 1998 album, is abold musical odyssey that for me represents one of the most successful collaborations in modernprogressive rock. The music of Explorers Club is a daring marriage of heavy but melodic neo-prog andtechnical prog metal, featuring lost of shredding and mind-bending soloing, complex arrangements andextended instrumental sections, polyrhythms, and a few truly experimental bits.I am certain that this album was conceived as one continuous piece of music, and while the albumtrack list features five distinct compositions, the former are actually connected and flow into eachother almost seamlessly, giving the impression of one gargantuan composition that goes throughseveral distinct sections, but remains true to the main album theme. Opening track 'Fate Speaks'sits at sixteen minutes and happens to be one of the most technically intense pieces on here - fromthe complex opening section, which is all-instrumental, to the excellent verses that come in at alater point and the scorchingly rapid solos of John Petrucci (and James Murphy, supposedly), this isa really strong prog metal suite that features Bret Douglas as the lead vocalist. The sound is epic,bombastic, celebratory and straight up wild, and fans of LTE and Dream Theater should reallyappreciate this massive track. 'Fading Fast' then introduces a more ethereal, keyboard-driven soundas well as some world music influences, which are explored brilliantly by Trent Gardner. Third track'No Returning' revisits the heavier sounds from the beginning of the album, as this part of thesuite serves as an almost all-instrumental middle section with excellent guitars and keys, while thesole vocal part is sang by James LaBrie. 'Time Enough', which is the fourth song on the album,explores a melodramatic new age sound and features some thoughtful lyrics, which are sang by D. C.Cooper, while the closing piece 'Last Call', returns to the main theme and expands it beautifully,concluding the record with a flamboyant streak of guitar pyrotechnics, occupying a good chunk of the11-minute-long final composition.'Age of Impact' is a fantastic project in my view - the complexity of the compositions, thegrandiose ideas, and the excellent execution should be seen as a treat by fans of prog rock and progmetal alike. The balanced vocal work and the cohesion of the entire work are commendable, too.However, unlike LTE or Dream Theater, the music of Explorers Club manages to evoke that classic progfeeling in a beautiful way, which is why I think it is one of the most underrated heavy prog gemfrom the late 1990s.
items._cn_summary: Heavy Prog与技术化前卫金属的深度融合之作，由Magellan核心Trent Gardner主导，联合Dream Theater吉他手John Petrucci、贝斯手Billy Sheehan、鼓手Terry Bozzio等摇滚界技术高手共同完成。专辑以五首连续乐章形式呈现，仿佛一部宏大的音乐史诗，融合了复杂编曲、器乐段落、复节奏结构以及世界音乐元素。多个声音主唱的设计增强了音乐的表现力与戏剧性，既有技术性极强的重兽段落，也有键盘驱动的空灵氛围段落。对于偏好实验与前卫音乐的用户而言，这张专辑在传统重金属于渐进摇滚框架内展现了相当程度的实验性与创新意识，尤其在曲式结构与音色探索上具有可听性。

items.body: Review by VianaProghead — Review N� 970Porcupine Tree is an English progressive rock band that was formed in 1987 in Hemel Hempstead, Hertfordshire. Their debut album 'On The Sunday Of Life'' was released in 1991. It's a selection of compositions from earlier unofficial cassette releases. The first 'full-fledged' album of Porcupine Tree isn't only an exhibition of the young artist's most interesting ideas, not only the essence of creative work concentrated in the psychedelic convention which Wilson undertook in the second half of the 80's, but is a compelling work, by all means enigmatic, mysterious, shrouded in an aura of unreality. It collects Wilson's favourite songs from those years into a double album. Listening in retrospect, we may well find pretty nonplussed at this highly experimental mixture of psychedelic and space rock, moving from ambient flute pieces to the sort of whimsical nonsense that wouldn't be out of place on the early Pink Floyd's releases.The line up 'On The Sunday Of Life'' is composed by Steven Wilson (vocals, guitar and other instruments like keyboards and programming). 'On The Sunday Of Life'' also has the participation of some other musicians. So, we also have here the presence of Malcolm Stocks 'Solomon St. Jemain' (vocals and additional guitars), Master Timothy Masters (oboe) and John Marshall (drums), as the guest musicians of the album.'On The Sunday Of Life'' has eighteen tracks. 'Music For The Head' is very short, a kind of an introduction to the album. It has a rather sinister tone, with some nice flute work to go with it. 'Jupiter Island' is from Wilson's adolescent days. It's a charming psychedelic tune with lyrics that features some fast paced drumming, apparently from a drum machine. The next pieces are two highly experimental short pieces. 'Third Eye Surfer' is a nice dissonant song with an odd metered drum improvisation along with synths and keys. The title track is an atmospheric piece dominated by the keyboards with a lot of sounds. Both pieces form two relaxed pieces on the album. 'The Nostalgia Factory' is the second song on the album including lyrics. This is a very nice psychedelic song with a great beat where the vocals sound distinctly due to the vocoder. The next two are yet more experimental pieces with some rather sinister spoken dialog. 'Space Transmission' is mostly spoken again through a vocoder. It's a very dark and ambient track. 'Message From A Self-Destructing Turnip' is another spoken piece, a very short ambient break piece. Both are psychedelic at its extreme. 'Radioactive Toy' is an interesting psychedelic epic with nice heavy guitar melodies and slowly pounding drums. It still is one of the favourite Porcupine Tree's songs played live as an encore. It has stood up to the test of time amazingly well. 'Nine Cats' is a nice acoustic track despite being very simple. It continues to emphasize the eclectic nature of the album. It became a fan's favourite that was rarely performed live. 'Hymn' is another short instrumental that has some strange vocal sounds and synths. It's more of a soundscape interlude between songs. 'Footprints' is also from Wilson's adolescent days. It also reminds me of Pink Floyd in Syd Barrett's era. It's another song with lyrics, guitar and synths. The next two tracks continue to absorb Pink Floyd's early influences. 'Linton Samuel Dawson' is awesomely weird and frenetic but very fun too. It's based on psychedelic drums and some mind blowing strange vocals through a vocoder. 'And The Swallows Dance Above The Sun' is another semi obscure odd track with a drum machine beat combined with ambient keyboards and vocals. 'Queen Quotes Crowley' is technically an instrumental. It has many psychedelic effects with some nice guitar work and where the vocals are in the reverse. The two next tracks are the final short instrumentals of this album. 'No Luck With Rabbits' is a very short experimental instrumental of synths, a kind of a soundscape between songs. 'Begonia Seduction Scene' is a lovely instrumental with some great acoustic guitar work and synths. 'This Long Silence' is a psychedelic up-tempo song that again features vocals through a vocoder. It follows the same style as some other songs, a good indication of what is to follow. 'It Will Rain For A Million Years' is another track that points the direction that the band would later take. There are hardly any lyrics on this song. Most of it is instrumental and ambient. It features a nice guitar work supported by a heavy rhythm, a good way to close the album.Conclusion: 'On The Sunday Of Life...' although in its moments heralds the later stylistic development of the band, as a whole is rather a sign of its time, a testimony to the band's interesting genesis. However, this doesn't diminish its value. It's a unique album, an extremely eclectic work. It treats this eclecticism as a method of surrealistic expression. It has its standout tracks, mainly 'Radioactive Toy', 'Nine Cats' and 'It Will Rain For A Million Years' that are worth the price of the purchase alone, but also features plenty of filler that you'll either enjoy for what it is or skip past every time. Nonetheless, for Porcupine Tree's fans, this album is of course a must to get to know the beginnings of the band and the roots of their later works. Still, I think it can be rather misleading for those who want to get to know the band. Anyhow and despite 'On The Sunday Of Life...' isn't as mature as later Porcupine Tree's stuff it still is recommendable.Prog is my Ferrari. Jem Godfrey (Frost*)
items._cn_summary: Porcupine Tree的《On the Sunday of Life...》是1991年的一张实验性渐进摇滚专辑，收录了乐队早期卡带时期的作品。这张双专辑融合了迷幻摇滚、太空摇滚、环境音乐与实验电子元素，从氛围长笛曲到使用Vocoder的人声曲目，再到沉重的吉他摇滚，呈现出极高的风格跨度。专辑中的《Radioactive Toy》被评价为乐队现场演出中最受欢迎的作品之一，展现出实验性与可听性的平衡。作为渐进摇滚领域的重要作品，它体现了Steven Wilson在1980年代后期对迷幻音乐的前卫探索，融合了爵士、电子与古典跨界元素，具有开创性意义。虽然发行年代较早，但对于实验音乐爱好者而言仍具有参考价值。

items.body: Review by Dapper~Blueberries — Bye bye Scott Kelly! You abusive loser.Ok, that aside, me and Neurosis have been in a pretty comfy relationship. I am not the biggest fanof them in comparison to their contemporaries like Isis, or Cult of Luna, but their releases havealways left a pleasant taste in my mouth. So, when I heard they were making a new studio work, adecade after their last one from 2016, I figured it wouldn't hurt to review them. Right?No it didn't hurt. In fact, this record is actually really great! An Undying Love for a BurningWorld is genuinely really solid stuff that I wouldn't argue with anyone if they say this was one oftheir favorites from the band.Initially, I was a bit cautious considering that their previous works, while good, didn't leave muchof an impression on me. But I think two key factors made me change my mind and wish to really reviewthis one.For one, the new vocalist, Aaron Turner of Isis fame is incredibly good, and a great fit forNeurosis' sound. I was quite surprised that Aaron was willing to fill the slot of vocalist,especially considering Isis disbanding in 2010. But, honestly, who better to fill the void than fora fellow veteran of post metal to set the new standard for the future of this legendary band?Not only that, but his vocals are just superb as ever. Seriously, I say his voice aged like a finewine. His screams are poignant; His growls are superb. Seriously, why wasn't he in this band sooneris what I'm wondering?The second factor, though, is atmosphere. Not like previous Neurosis records couldn't have anoticeable vibe, but they weren't always their strong suit, even in the post metal space. Honestlythe only one that really stuck out to me was Souls at Zero. But An Undying Love for a Burning World?Hoo boy this thing is juicy with tension. The band still plays how they'd play years ago, but theyreally push themselves by really going noticeably away from sludge metal, and into horizons thatfeel like a heavier version of that of Godspeed You! Black Emperor, whilst also combining elementsfrom Isis, and Coil to really make it all work. It's genuinely such a vibe, and makes for somereally impressive music.The best track in this regard is easily Blind, in my opinion. This is probably the most post metalsong that has ever been post metal'd since Locust Star.Though, this record isn't perfect for me. Don't get me wrong, if this record was a person, I'd dateit, but at the same time it does suffer a tiny, minute, almost inconsequential problem that sort ofsours the pot, and that's Last Light, the big 16 minute track of the record. It's not a bad song,far from it. But at the same time, I feel like it doesn't quite END this record the best. You knowthat feeling you get when you have a show or series that you really, really like, and the lastepisode comes out and you aren't totally wowed by it? That's this song for me. It's definitely good,as it has a great middle with two decent beginnings and ends, but nothing that really screamsfinale, if anything.Heck, sometimes I get confused and think there is something more after it. But no. Honestly I thinkthe previous track of In The Waiting Hours would be a better end for this record. If they swappedthose around, than I think the record would be near perfect.Other than that, though, An Undying Love for a Burning World is certainly one of Neurosis' standoutrecords now, at least for me. It has depth, beauty, and heaviness galore that really makes me wantto see what they'll do next. Certainly a recommendation.Best tracks: First Red Rays, Blind
items._cn_summary: 这张2026年专辑是Post Metal领域的重量级作品，由前Isis成员Aaron Turner担任新主唱，带来成熟且富有表现力的人声演绎。专辑显著偏离传统Sludge Metal框架，融入Godspeed You! Black Emperor式的宏大氛围感，同时借鉴Isis的旋律性和Coil的暗潮元素，营造出紧张而厚重的听觉空间。最大亮点在于氛围营造，16分钟的长篇曲目"Last Light"虽整体扎实，但作为结尾的冲击力略显不足。专辑在保持Neurosis一贯深沉的情感张力同时，成功开辟了更具实验性和交响感的声场，是Post Metal乐迷和偏好暗潮氛围的听众值得关注之作。

Day two of our celebration of Miles Davis at 100. See day one here.On the Corner (Columbia Records, 1972)


    
        Abrasive, Alcoholic, Anarchic, Anticlimax, Aphrodisiac, Arrogant,

        Psychotropic, Quirky, Quixotic, Raw, Reckless, Rusty, Saturated,
        Self-indulgent, Sexy, Spiraling, Syncretic, Telluric, Temperamental,
        Timeless, Toxic, Uncanny, Uncompromising, Unruly, Vibrant, Visionary,
        Vulgar, Wicked, Xenomorphic, Yucky, Zippy: QUINTESSENTIAL, BLACK, MILES. - Ferruccio Martinotti  



    ESP (Columbia Records, 1965)


    
        Miles Davis’s second great quintet put a fantastic four behind the great
        leader: Wayne Shorter, Herbie Hancock, Ron Carter, and Tony Williams.
        Their 1965 ESP is the perfect result.  Miles was the philosopher’s
        stone: put him in the presence of a potential genius stuck in a rut, two
        virtuosos coming to the studio with mediocre melodies, or two simple
        chords longing for each other and the right hands on the keyboard…and you
        got pure gold.
    


    
        It helps if you have a crush on Shorter and Hancock.  If you have been
        touched by the former’s Juju, or the latter’s Empyrean Isles you will
        feel your heart fluttering awake.  The mood is pensive, sadly romantic
        (but in a good way), and always extending the witch’s finger.  It
        doesn’t get better than this, just different and rarely as delicious.  - Kenneth Blanchard---

Miles Davis and the Modern Jazz Giants (Prestige, 1956)Miles Davis and the Modern Jazz Giants was the first Miles
    Davis record I ever heard. It was a well-played LP in my Dad’s collection
    that I stumbled upon in my first year of college and for some reason, I
    decided to spin it. This was almost my first encounter with jazz at all —
    except some big band stuff in Abbott and Costello movies — and I would find
    it hard to convey the immediate wonderment I felt listening to Milt
    Jackson’s opening to “The Man I Love” (take 2).

    Milt Jackson’s vibes weren’t the point to that track, and they're not the
    point to this encomium, but, like the Yellow Brick Road, that opening led me
    to an extraordinary, life-changing experience. I still wonder why nobody
    plays vibes like that, and I still wonder what it is about Miles’ non-muted
    take on the melody that hearing it — and Monk, Red Garland, and Coltrane —
    was like nothing before or since, for me.
 Tutu
    (Warner Bros., 1986) The first new Miles Davis record that came out after hearing that was Tutu. Forty years separate me from that first listen, and
    thirty years separate Tutu from “The Man I Love.” I still enjoy Tutu quite a
    lot. All the tunes were written by or with producer/bassist, Marcus Miller —
    much as all the tunes from Miles’ 2nd quintet were written by Wayne Shorter
    — but there was no mistaking that Miles led the sessions and that it was
    Miles Davis music.
    I would be lying if I said Tutu was as high in my estimation as the Prestige
    record, but the things that make Miles' music the ineffable thing it is are
    present in both cases. There’s a sweetness and melancholy in the
    ever-present harmon mute. His melodies are treated just so, and his
    improvisations seem inevitable. Also, possibly because of the space he
    leaves or the example he sets, he improves every musician he works with
    (except maybe Monk, but there’s a story behind that). So much time has
    passed, but this music still fires off my endorphins. Wonderful.- Gary Chapin---
    Ascenseur pour l'échafaud Soundtrack (Fontana, 1958)Paris is the perfect city to film at night, in black and white, with its streetlights and shadows in soft focus. It’s the perfect city to film beautiful Jeanne Moreau as she walks without direction searching for her missing lover, passing brightly lit cafés and dimly lit alleys, stumbling in a daze through traffic.
      And Miles Davis’s plaintive trumpet makes the perfect music to accompany
    her, the perfect music to furtively whisper “Je t’aime”, the perfect music
    to commit a murder for love…and the perfect music to get stuck in an
    elevator while trying to make your escape.

    Miles Davis recorded the soundtrack for Louis Malle’s debut film Ascenseur
    pour l'échafaud (Elevator To The Gallows) by improvising while watching the
    film. It’s a great film in its own right, a terrific blend of noir tropes,
    and it’s one of the first films of the French New Wave. But it’s the
    soundtrack that makes it an all-time classic. - Richard Blute

items._cn_summary: 本文为Miles Davis百年纪念专辑系列的第二篇评论，涵盖《On the Corner》（1972）、《ESP》（1965）和《Miles Davis and the Modern Jazz Giants》（1956）三张专辑，横跨传统爵士、Modal Jazz及融合实验阶段。Miles Davis作为爵士乐史上最具革命性的音乐家之一，其作品与用户偏好的学院派爵士高度契合，1972年《On the Corner》更融合了摇滚、funk等元素，具备显著的前卫实验性。乐评质量较高，包含个人聆听经历与专业分析，但由于三张专辑均来自Columbia Records与Prestige等主流大厂，且Miles Davis本身属欧美主流艺术家，在用户偏好体系中小众实验属性相对有限，整体评分处于中高区间。

items._cn_summary: 加纳裔澳大利亚音乐人Genesis Owusu的新专辑延续了其跨流派风格的探索，从灵魂乐、说唱、摇滚到电子与爵士的边界地带自由游走。作为澳大利亚独立音乐界的代表性人物，Owusu的作品常被形容为声音层面的社会批判与文化抵抗。专辑延续了2021年《Smiling with No Teeth》与2023年《Struggler》奠定的高评价基调，在实验性与可听性之间保持平衡。加纳背景为作品注入非洲音乐元素，与澳大利亚当代独立音乐场景形成独特对话。The Quietus将其评为年度重要的声音创作，体现了作品在实验性、社会批判与艺术表达上的综合完成度。

items.body: Review by siLLy puPPy — The band released its sole album BIZITAKO GAUZEK (Things Lived) in 1978 on the Elkar label and citedthe big players in the English scene as the primary focal points for references. Pink Floyd, Yes,King Crimson, Genesis and even Emerson, Lake & Palmer provided the blueprints for which SAKREcrafted its own unique brand of symphonic rock and although the band is noted in history for beingone of the few to actually engage in a more rock oriented style of prog, BIZITAKO GAUZEK still findsmany moments of softer folky moments it's just that they are not derived from the band's own uniqueisolate heritage and therefore SAKRE was much closer to other Spanish and Italian symphonic progbands with romantic lead vocals, dreamy sweeping synthesizers, melodic guitar riffing, group vocalharmonies and theatrical concept based compositions.As one of the first prog bands to emerge after the fall of the Franco dictatorship, SAKRE honed itschops on the live circuit for years before recording its sole release. Taking on the truecharacteristics of a 70s prog band, SAKRE delivered a full blown dramatic concept album with emotivemovements that spanned ten tracks but sadly limited to a mere 34 minutes. The band has cited suchclassics as The Who's "Quadraphenia" and Genesis' "The Lamb That Lies Down On Broadway" as keyreferences for the subject matter which in this case tackles the psychological state of a person'slife and the trials and tribulations which sort of qualifies them as an early prototype of the worldof neo-prog which would soon adopt the same techniques and become the first official prog revivalgenre. Also like a great prog release this one is fortified with lots of bold time signatureworkouts, a trait eschewed by many of the mellow Basque folk crowds crafting more subtle versions ofprog folk.While the opening "Erreberentzia (Ohiko Dantza)" insinuates yet another dreamy folk album emergingfrom northeastern Spain with some traditional wind instrument and a ritualistic drum beat withoutany accompanying instrumentation, the following "Orain" quickly dispels those assumptions anddisplays a more symphonic rock approach with guitar-fueled riffing and the notable absence of anyflute sounds whatsoever. Tracks like "Ezengaino" fire on all prog cylinders with Squire-esque bassgrooves, beefy organ swells accompanied by Emerson keyboard wizardry and jazzy drum rolls punctuatedwith wily time signature off shoots courtesy of the early Yes years. The album loses no momentum asit continues delivering high quality tracks that culminate with the satisfying climactic closer"Bilatzea" leaving me to wish this album was a bit longer as there are really no stagnant moments tobe found. While perusing through the various Basque progressive acts that spanned a short period of just a fewyears, this band clearly stood out sounding nothing like Haizea, Izukaitz, Magdalena, Enbor and therest. Only Lisker engaged in a more rock oriented approach. This is an excellent album marred onlyby its rarity of only being available as a first print vinyl edition and of course that the conceptis unintelligible to all except native Basque speakers. Musically though this sounds most similar tomore guitar oriented symphonic prog bands from Italy given the rhythmic flow of it all even thoughthe English scene was cited as the key wellsprings of inspiration. All in all this is one of myfaves to emerge from the lesser known Basque scene which stood out of the homogenous pack like asore thumb but all the best for it.
items._cn_summary: 这是一张1978年发行于西班牙巴斯克地区的交响前卫摇滚专辑，乐队SAKRE受英式前卫摇滚巨头Pink Floyd、Yes、King Crimson、Genesis及ELP深刻影响，创作出一张心理探索主题的概念专辑。作为佛朗哥政权垮台后最早的前卫乐队之一，专辑融合了巴斯克传统民谣元素，如仪式性鼓点与传统管乐器，同时展现复杂的时间签名变化、爵士鼓滚奏及模拟合成器编排。专辑仅34分钟却包含10首曲目，呈现紧凑而完整的艺术表达。作为巴斯克地区独特的文化产物，专辑在西班牙与意大利交响摇滚传统中占据一席之地，被视为早期neo-prog的原型作品，在前卫摇滚发展脉络中具有研究价值。

items.body: Review by Matti — Painovoima I ("Gravity I") is the latest release of the Finnish group Avaruusasema, the first part of the album pair which sort of explains the brevity. Containing six tracks between 2 and 7 minutes length, it clocks only about 29 minutes. My actual rating is 3,5 and I feel that rounding it down feels more suitable despite some very strong stuff heard here. The band with space-oriented roots still has a space rock vibe, even though (since 2024's Kilonova) their songwriting has become a bit more down to earth, at places reminding me of the other Imatra-based band, Crossover Prog act Aching Hands, also featuring vocalist-guitarist Heikki P�yhi�, keyboard player Lauri Kuosa and bassist Pekka Ranta. Here they share writing duties (both jointly and individually) for most of the material, The exceptions being the two final songs.Ranta's instrumental composition 'Ruuhka' ("Traffic jam") is, against its title, actually rather spatial. serene and ambientish, and it's followed seamlessly by the pulsative and dynamic P�yhi� piece 'Hopeinen Taunus'. The song about a car ride is poignantly monotonous in melody but it works nicely. The joint composition 'Aallot' ("The Waves") is a groovy pop-rock song where especially the funk-flavoured bass and the TOTO reminding vocals sound really good. The female vocalist Heli Valkama adds a brief spoken part. Perhaps the six-minute length is not quite as justified as it ought to be on such a short album, and the whole A side feels slightly undermeasured of material. The B side is much more gratifying also for prog oriented ears. P�yhi� and Kuosa composition 'Ilma ja tuli' ("Air and fire") gives Heli the main vocals, and she handles them excellently. Even the rap vocal section is good. I love this strong and intense song (3:08) and wish it was twice as long! 'Myrskypatsas' ("Storm pillar") is written by the other bassist and backing vocalist Juuso Partanen who also sings it and plays the acoustic guitar. The song is relatively melancholic and slow-tempo, and the guest appearance of a French horn finishes its sonic elegance. The final piece 'Palavat t�hdet' ("Burning stars"), composed by guitarist Roy Heino, is the album's proggiest song that combines Tabula Rasa reminding emotional charge with a space-rocking, Pink Floyd (say, Meddle or Animals) seasoned intensity.Let's wait for the sequel. Together the two probably would make a gorgeous long album with a good dose of stylistic diversity. In theory the brevity is not a sin, but as I said, the A side is not on par with the superb B side, hence rounding down my 3,5 stars.
items._cn_summary: 芬兰乐队Avaruusasema的《Painevoima I》是一张融合多种风格的折衷前卫摇滚专辑。乐队以空间摇滚为根基，在2024年后转向更接地气的创作路线，作品中融合了流行摇滚、放克贝斯、氛围音乐及渐进式摇滚等元素。专辑A面以空间氛围和汽车主题歌曲为主，整体略显单薄；B面则更为出色，特别是《Ilma ja tuli》展现了强烈的情感张力，女主唱Heli Valkama的演绎尤为出色，融合说唱段落亦不显突兀。结尾曲目《Palavat tähtet》最具前瞻性，将情感表达与Pink Floyd式的空间摇滚强度相结合。专辑虽仅29分钟，但B面的艺术成就足以证明乐队的实验精神与非主流音乐地区（北欧）的独特视角，整体符合实验/前卫音乐爱好者的审美取向。
